input.quote: 10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 10.3 is only a successors-and-assigns binding-effect clause: it does not say who may assign, imposes no consent standard, and gives us no express affiliate or M&A carve-out; HDI is equally free to assign, including to one of our competitors. There is no change-of-control language anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "change of control" and the termination provisions in Section 4 return nothing), so no Vendor exit right exists today but the point is unconfirmed. The clause therefore fails the fallback (no successor-assignment right with notice, no consent standard for other assignments) and we have drafted to the preferred position with a single added paragraph in Section 10.3, preserving the existing binding-effect language verbatim.

proposal.summary: Add assignment rights and consent standard to Section 10.3
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10.3 only binds successors and assigns and says nothing about who may assign. We added our customary affiliate/M&A assignment right, a consent requirement (not unreasonably withheld) on HDI's side with no assignment to our competitors, and confirmation that a change of control of the Company gives HDI no termination right.

ops.text: The Company may assign this Agreement without HDI's consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets, and no change of control of the Company shall give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement. HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, and in no event to a competitor of the Company.

mappings.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
